record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Numerical methods for nonperiodic nonlocal problems
record.original_question: Is there a general numerical method that can efficiently solve the nonlocal bounded-domain problems from Section 2.2.2 when the boundary conditions are not periodic, so that one no longer relies on pseudo-spectral methods tailored to periodic domains?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 55. Is there a general technique to efficiently solve nonlocal problems of the form appearing in Section 2.2.2 subject to boundary conditions that are not of the periodic type?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider nonlocal reaction–diffusion–advection equations on a bounded spatial domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of the general form
$$\partial_t u(x,t) = D\,\Delta u(x,t) - \nabla\!\cdot\!\big(u(x,t)\,\mathbf{v}[u](x,t)\big) + f(u(x,t)), \qquad x\in\Omega,\ t>0,$$
where the advective velocity $\mathbf{v}[u]$ is a nonlocal functional of $u$, typically given by a convolution
$$\mathbf{v}[u](x,t) = \int_{\Omega} K(x,y)\,g(u(y,t))\,dy$$
with a (possibly singular or anisotropic) kernel $K$ modeling perception or cognitive averaging over a neighborhood of $x$. Assume the problem is supplemented with non-periodic boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega$ (for instance, no-flux/Neumann, Dirichlet, or Robin conditions), so that pseudo-spectral methods based on Fourier expansions on a periodic torus are not directly applicable.

Question: Does there exist a general numerical method (independent of the specific choice of kernel $K$ and nonlinearities $f$, $g$, and of the geometry of $\Omega$) that efficiently and accurately solves such nonlocal evolution problems on bounded domains under non-periodic boundary conditions, with computational complexity and accuracy comparable to what pseudo-spectral methods achieve in the periodic setting?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a collection of open problems on PDE models with nonlocal perception. No subsequent work resolving the general question of an efficient, kernel-agnostic numerical scheme for nonlocal bounded-domain problems under non-periodic boundary conditions was located; partial progress exists via finite-volume, finite-element, and reflected-kernel approaches in specific settings, but no general method matching pseudo-spectral efficiency has been established.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including the efficient numerical solution of nonlocal bounded-domain problems with non-periodic boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open.
